toml:
# Telecom timing reference: a rubidium clock that loses its Global Navigation Satellite
# System (GNSS) reference and holds over for 24 hours, checked against the masks of the
# International Telecommunication Union Telecommunication Standardization Sector (ITU-T).
#
# The record is 25 hours at one sample per second. For the first hour the clock is
# disciplined, and its time error is 1 ns of white phase noise. At 3 600 s the GNSS
# reference is lost and the clock free-runs for 24 hours with:
#   - white, flicker and (where the fit needs it) random-walk frequency noise, fitted to
#     the datasheet's Allan-deviation maxima and scaled to lie at or above every one;
#   - linear frequency aging at the datasheet's monthly figure;
#   - a daily temperature cycle of +/-2 K (an illustrative indoor swing) through the
#     datasheet's temperature bound, read linearly as a worst case.
# The oscillator figures come from the Microchip 8040C Rubidium Frequency Standard
# datasheet (DS00003047A). How they become a noise model is MODELLED: see the report's
# `oscillator` block and docs/TELECOM-TIMING.md.
#
# What the run answers: how long this clock stays inside each time-error budget, and
# whether the record meets the ePRTC-A holdover requirement of ITU-T G.8272.1 (a time
# error that may rise from 30 ns to 100 ns over the holdover period). A rubidium clock is
# not the caesium-class reference that requirement assumes, so a FAIL there is the
# expected, informative answer. PRTC-A (ITU-T G.8272) is a LOCKED-mode requirement; it is
# applied here as a comparison only, and the report states that condition beside it.
#
# Not a conformance test and not a measurement of any unit.
kind = "telecom-timing"
seed = 20260925
masks = ["eprtc-a-holdover", "prtc-a"]

[holdover]
oscillator = "rubidium"
gnss_loss_s = 3600.0
duration_s = 90000.0
sample_interval_s = 1.0
locked_te_sigma_ns = 1.0
initial_frequency_offset = 0.0
temperature_amplitude_k = 2.0
temperature_period_s = 86400.0
# ITU-T G.8272.1 Table 3: under 6 days locked, the holdover period H is 70 000 s.
locked_duration_days = 5.0

# Budgets: each is a figure an ITU-T Recommendation states.
[[budgets]]
name = "ePRTC default max|TE_HO|"
max_abs_te_ns = 100.0
source = "ITU-T G.8272.1 (2024) Amd. 1 (07/2025) clause 8.3.1"

[[budgets]]
name = "network holdover allocation, short GNSS interruption"
max_abs_te_ns = 400.0
source = "ITU-T G.8271.1 (2022) Amd. 3 (05/2025) Table V.1, failure scenario (b) (an example allocation)"

[[budgets]]
name = "network limit at reference point C"
max_abs_te_ns = 1100.0
source = "ITU-T G.8271.1 (2022) Amd. 3 (05/2025) clause 7.3.1 (max|TE_L|, compared unfiltered)"

[[budgets]]
name = "end application, accuracy class 4"
max_abs_te_ns = 1500.0
source = "ITU-T G.8271 (03/2020) Amd. 1 (08/2024) Table 1, class 4"
summary: telecom-timing: max|TE| 603.2 ns over 90000 s; eprtc-a-holdover FAIL, prtc-a FAIL; 100 ns budget exceeded after 8206 s (MODELLED)
